name: Taj Mahal
description: A white marble mausoleum commissioned in 1632 by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, recognised as one of the finest examples of Mughal architecture.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Red Fort Complex (Lal Qila)
description: The historic fort complex in Old Delhi that served as the primary residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years and the site of India's annual Independence Day flag-hoisting ceremony.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Qutb Minar
description: A 72.5 metre red sandstone minaret built in 1193 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, marking the commencement of the Delhi Sultanate and the first garden city complex in India.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Ajanta Caves
description: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments cut into a horseshoe-shaped gorge on the Waghora River, renowned for their wall paintings and sculptures spanning roughly two centuries of Buddhist art.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Sun Temple, Konark
description: A 13th-century chariot-shaped temple dedicated to the sun god Surya, renowned for its monumental stone-carved wheels and intricate narrative reliefs.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Sun Temple, Konark
description: A 13th-century chariot-shaped temple dedicated to the sun god Surya, renowned for its monumental stone-carved wheels and intricate narrative reliefs.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: A group of Hindu and Jain temples built between 950 and 1050 CE, celebrated for their elaborate Nagara-style architecture and richly carved sculptures depicting celestial and earthly life.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Elephanta Caves
description: A network of rock-cut cave temples on an island in Mumbai Harbour, primarily dedicated to Shiva and dating from the 6th to 8th centuries, featuring monumental sculptural panels including the famous Trimurti.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site; ASI-protected monument

name: Jama Masjid
description: One of the largest mosques in India, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656. The mosque's courtyard can accommodate over 25,000 people.
preservation_context: UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of Red Fort Complex); ASI-protected monument
